corpusSummary: Across 2026 publications, large language models are studied as both analytical tools and social actors. Researchers explore methodological uses in policy, climate, health, and humanities, while examining human–AI interaction, trust, embodiment, ethics, and governance. The corpus highlights equity, safety, and literacy considerations, and notes persistent concerns around mis/disinformation, anthropomorphism, and access disparities in diverse settings.

themes.name: AI as a methodological instrument for social science
themes.description: Papers position LLMs as analytical tools and theory-builders across policy, climate, health, and humanities, enabling cross-domain transfer, framing analyses, and agentic simulations while raising validity and ethics concerns.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and social dynamics
themes.description: Research investigates trust, perceived humanness vs. empathy, AI embodiment, and how social networks and contexts shape AI adoption and the effectiveness of AI assistance.

themes.name: AI in education: literacy, tutoring, and assessment
themes.description: Studies examine AI-assisted tutoring, scaffolding, and learning analytics, as well as AI literacy development and assessment integrity in educational contexts.

themes.name: Equity, health governance, and ethical accountability
themes.description: Work focuses on equity-first governance for digital health AI, fairness in services, clinical safety, and frameworks to audit bias and cultural adequacy in AI deployments.
